editorial:
Imagine your favorite childhood toys suddenly becoming obsolete because of a screen. That is exactly what happens here when Bonnie gets a Lilypad tablet. You get to see Woody, Buzz, and Jessie struggle to keep Bonnie's attention while she spends all her time staring at a digital device. It feels like a throwback to the first movie where the toys are terrified of being replaced, but this time the enemy is technology. The vibe is super nostalgic but also feels fresh because it deals with something we all see in real life today.

What really works is how the movie balances the laughs with some genuinely sad moments. The action scenes involving the tablet are creative, and the pacing keeps you moving quickly toward the end. While some parts feel a bit too similar to previous films, the heart of the story is still there. You should definitely watch this with your kids or your parents for a full family night.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up when the toys realize they cannot beat the tablet, so they learn to work with it. They find a way to integrate their play with the digital world, showing Bonnie that real friends are better than apps. In the final twist, the tablet actually helps them find a lost toy from Bonnie's past. Everyone reunites in a big hug, and Bonnie learns to balance her screen time with her imagination.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Pixar and family adventures
